transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My doctor thought I should come in. She says I’ve gotten too thin. I mean… my work pants are hanging pretty loose now. I notice that. But when the scale’s lower, part of me still feels… relieved, I guess.
Do you ever worry about gaining weight?
Yes… I do. If I eat something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I get scared the rest of the day that it’s going to show on me. I’ll keep checking myself and thinking I need to make up for it somehow.
How often do you think about your weight during the day?

A lot, I guess. It’s kind of there in the background. If I feel small and… tidy, I feel like I’m doing okay. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach seems even a little full, then I start thinking I’ve let myself go.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within an hour?
I don’t think so… not like a big amount all at once. I usually don’t let it get to that.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No… I don’t really do that. I might feel upset after eating, but I don’t make myself throw up.
Do you ever exercise excessively to burn off calories?
I’m not sure I’d call it excessive. I’m on my feet a lot anyway with work, and… I don’t really think of it that way.
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while eating?
I don’t really know… I don’t think of it that way. I’m usually trying to be careful, so… no, not really.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten an amount of food that's larger than what most people would eat in a short period of time?
I don’t think so… I mean, I don’t usually eat very much at once, so… no, I haven’t really noticed that.
Have you ever felt like you've eaten an amount of food that's larger than what most people would eat in a short period of time, even if it's not all at once?
I don’t think so. I mean… I might feel like I ate more than I meant to sometimes, but not more than other people would, I don’t think.
Do you often limit yourself to only eating certain foods or avoiding certain types of food?

Yeah… I guess I do. I make dinner for my husband and my mother-in-law, but when it’s time for me to eat, I’ll just have coffee, or some vegetables… maybe half a piece of toast. I tell myself that’s enough.
How much weight have you lost since you first started feeling relieved when the scale was lower?
I… I don’t really know the exact number. My doctor says I’ve gotten too thin, and my work pants are hanging loose now. But… when the scale is lower, part of me still feels relieved.
Have you ever eaten a normal or larger amount of food without trying to restrict or compensate for it afterwards?

Not really without thinking about it after. If I eat something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I… I spend the rest of the day worried it’s going to show on me. I keep checking myself and thinking I need to make up for it somehow.
Have you ever felt like you've eaten an amount of food that's larger than what most people would eat under similar circumstances?
I don’t think so… not larger than most people, no. I mean, sometimes it feels like too much to me, but I don’t know what other people would call a lot.
Have you ever had a time when you ate more food than you planned, and then felt like you needed to restrict your eating afterwards to make up for it?
Yes… I guess so. If I eat more than I meant to, especially something like biscuits or pasta, I get scared it’s going to show on me. Then I keep looking at myself and thinking I should cut back after.
Do you think you would still be worried about gaining weight if you couldn't see yourself in the mirror or didn't know what you weighed?

Yes… I think I would. Even if I couldn’t see it right then, I’d still be worried it was showing somehow, especially after something heavier like pasta or biscuits. I’d still feel like I had to make up for it.
Do you think your weight and body shape are the main things that determine your self-worth?

I suppose… yes, more than I’d like to admit. If I feel small and tidy, like I’m keeping myself together, then I feel all right. But if my stomach looks even a little full in the mirror, I feel like I’ve let myself go.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is because you're worried about losing control while eating?

I suppose it’s partly that… but mostly if I eat something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I spend the rest of the day worrying it’ll show on me. Then I keep checking and thinking I need to make up for it somehow.
Is your decision on what to eat mostly based on trying not to gain weight?

Yes… mostly, I suppose. I tend to think about whether it’ll make me gain. If it’s something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I get scared it’ll show on me, and then I keep checking and thinking I need to make up for it.
Do you feel like you are eating in a way that is mostly driven by a desire to not gain weight?

Yes… I think so. If I have something heavier, like pasta or biscuits, I get frightened it’ll show on me. Then I spend the rest of the day checking myself and thinking I ought to make up for it somehow.
Is your main goal in restricting your food intake to avoid gaining weight or to achieve a specific body shape?
Mostly to not gain, I think… or not have it show on me. If I eat something like biscuits or pasta, I end up checking myself all day and thinking I need to make up for it somehow.
